entry.dc:title: Chromosomal abnormalities in soft coal open-cast mining workers
entry.dc:creator: Šrám R.J.
entry.dc:description: Chromosome aberration tests on cultured peripheral blood lymphocytes were carried out in two groups of open-cast mining workers engaged in stripping operations (Group I) and digging operations (Group II), in a group of coal cleaning plant workers used as a positive control, and in a group of nonexposed subjects serving as matching controls. Peripheral blood samples in group I and group II miners were collected in March and June of 1984, the antimutagenic potential of long-term prophylactic vitamin administrations (1 g of ascorbic acid given daily for a period of 3 months and 100 mg of vitamin A a day for two 5-day cycles) initiated after the first blood sampling was tested in group II miners. The frequency of aberrant cells (% AB.C.) found in the cultured lymphocytes of group I miners was increased at both times of measurement (2.41 % AB.C. and 2.29 % AB.C.), in group II miners given the vitamin prophylaxis it dropped significantly (P>0.01) from the initial 3.16 % AB.C. in March to 1.77 % AB.C. in June, and in the group of coal cleaning plant workers (1.30 % AB.C.) it was more or less equal to that of matching controls (1.21 % AB.C.). Implicity, coal dust alone can hardly be made responsible for the rise in % AB.C. It appears that the increase in frequency of chromosome aberrations observed in soft coal open-cast mining workers rather reflects an increased risk of genetic injury due to exposure to ever-present fumes and fire hazards that may give rise to the mutagenic chemicals belonging to a class of polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons. The antimutagenic effect of ascorbic acid prophylaxis was characterized by a significant drop in % AB.C. and a speed-up of the lymphocyte cell cycle expressed as the proliferating rate index (PRI) whose value rose from the original 1.41 to 1.69, thus reaching the PRI value of matching controls (1.63). © 1985.

entry.dc:title: (The open-cast mining of coal in France).
entry.dc:creator: Bieau J.
entry.dc:description: Describes open-cast mines in the 'Centre-Midi' region of southwestern France. Summarizes the situation in the fields of production, reserves, on-going prospection and financial results.-from English summary

entry.dc:title: SURFACE MINER 3000 SM/3800 SM. A NEW MACHINE FOR OPEN-CAST MINING.
entry.dc:creator: Goergen H.
entry.dc:description: The machines have operational limits in soft rock with solidified seams as a result of their inadequate cutting power, or in hard rock containing thin mineral seams due to their lack of selectivity. This results in high costs when clearing interstratified hard seams by special operations, or alternatively mining losses. A newly developed open-cast mining machine, which can assist in the elimination of these disadvantages is described.

entry.dc:title: GIANT OPEN-CAST COAL AND LIGNITE MINES IN INDIA.
entry.dc:creator: Srinivasan H.
entry.dc:description: Coal mining in India is nearly 150 years old, but mechanized open-cast mining is of recent origin. A start was made in the early fifties with Sir Lindsay Parkinson, a U. K. firm of contractors being commissioned to operate the first large mechanized open-cast mine in the East Bokaro coal fields in Bihar State.

entry.dc:title: INDIAN MINING CURRENT STATE-OF-THE-ART OF BULK SOLIDS HANDLING.
entry.dc:creator: Basu A.K.
entry.dc:description: The Neyveli lignite mine, the only one of its kind in India, has adopted the fully-mechanised open-cast mining system using bucket wheel excavator technology to handle an excavated overburden volume of 35 Mt/a for a lignite production of 6. 5 Mt/a. The crawler-mounted bucket wheel excavator (BWE) operates in terracing cuts. The travelling transfer-feeder connected to the BWE delivers the material excavated from the face into a transfer hopper, which moves over the fast running receiving belt conveyor line.

entry.dc:title: Sediment yield estimation and the design of sediment control structures in rural Africa.
entry.dc:creator: Ward A.
entry.prism:publicationName: Challenges in African Hydrology and Water Resources Proc Harare Symposium 1984
entry.dc:description: In the last few decades agriculture, urbanization and open-cast mining activities have expanded rapidly in southern Africa. Discusses procedures for determining sediment yields and presents a computer based technique for determining surface runoff and sediment yields from a rural catchment. Application of the model is discussed and the selection and design of several sediment control measures is outlined. -from Authors

entry.dc:title: Surface erosion and sediment control at open-cast mines in southern Africa.
entry.dc:creator: Ward A.
entry.prism:publicationName: Challenges in African Hydrology and Water Resources Proc Harare Symposium 1984
entry.dc:description: Large-scale open-cast mining disturbs large areas of land which need to be restored. Sediment yield from these areas can be several hundred times greater than from undisturbed areas. This paper presents an outline of surface erosion problems associated with coal mining operations. -from Authors

entry.dc:title: (The interrelationship between coal power stations and the environment).
entry.dc:creator: Weidlich H.
entry.dc:description: In brown coal mining, the installation of plant in a territory and the recognition of its diverse relationships is, next to optimal heat technological considerations, of great significance. It requires inter-related ways of looking at substance and energy flow regarding open-cast mining. Using examples of water-cooling and fuel provision, problems of air purification and waste management relating to incurred residues from burning processes are discussed.-translated by C.Wilson environmental pollution fuel supply.

entry.dc:creator: Krummsdorf A.

entry.dc:title: Giving back the land - a look at open-cast mining.
entry.dc:creator: Thompson G.
entry.dc:description: Shows the dominance of minerals in the South African economy. Coal is a major growth factor in this. Illuminates open-cast coal and copper mining, and the way land is reclaimed afterwards. In particular, reclamation at the Palabora copper mines is described. -D.J.Davis

entry.dc:title: Some anthropogenic changes in the landscape structure of the Pernik Basin.
entry.dc:creator: Kandev T.
entry.dc:description: The relief suffers from the open-cast mining of coal, resulting in disturbances of the natural forms and the creation of new earth shapes. The pollution of air and water by the steelworks, the power station and the other industrial plants surpasses the permissible limits. The soil cover changes due to accelerated erosion and deforestation of the region, building on fertile land and pollution by heavy metals from traffic and industries. -from Abstracts of Bulgarian Scientific Literature

entry.dc:title: Additional Recovery of Valuable Minerals and Secondary Elements from an Iron-ore Deposit as a Measure for Improving Profitability.
entry.dc:creator: Feik H.
entry.dc:description: Open-cast mining in the primary magnetite iron-ore deposit will gradually reach zones where overburden predominantly consists of transitional ores which include large portions of martite and hematite. Modern equipment for high-intensity magnetic separation permits the recovery of these valuable minerals. Apart from concentrating the iron minerals from these two zones of the deposit to mainly sinter- and pellet-feed, such processing also serves to reduce the sulfur content, which is related to pyrite. The pyrite features significant copper and cobalt contents, which can be recovered by a combination of mechanical dressing and metallurgical treatment. These measures not only improve the economy of the mining operation but at the same time less destructive and more efficient exploitation of the ore deposit.

entry.dc:title: Changes in the groundwater due to surface mining
entry.dc:creator: Libicki J.
entry.dc:description: Open-cast mining operations conducted below groundwater table often affect the drawdown of the water table over large areas which as a consequence changes the natural regional hydrological balance. Remedial measures may include construction of new water intakes, and changes in the land usage may be necessary. Tipping of wastes (most often coal wastes and ashes) affects ground water pollution. Instead of removal of effects, preventive methods are recommended. © 1982 Springer-Verlag.

entry.dc:title: COMPARATIVE DANGER OF DIFFERENT KINDS OF CURRENT.
entry.dc:creator: Shchutskii V.
entry.dc:description: Reports statistics of electrotrauma in dc and ac installations during open-cast mining operations 1964-1979. Use of thyristor drives, insulation monitoring and lack of specifications for rectified current, control-angle current and mixed current (e. g. dc superposed on sinusoidal current, or mutually superposed sinusoidal currents of different frequency) prompt this comparative study for development of Standards. Tests were performed on a group of 40 volunteers.

entry.dc:title: PLAIN SPHERICAL THRUST BEARINGS FOR 45,000 KN AXIAL LOAD AND 4,500 KN RADIAL LOAD.
entry.dc:creator: Stoecklein W.
entry.dc:description: The total weight of 57 eight-wheel electric locomotives would correspond to the load to be transmitted by the plain spherical bearing mounted to the support structure of a giant travelling overburden conveyor bridge. With a length of 475 meters the conveyor bridge spans the open cut of the brown coal open-cast mining area Jaenschwalde near Cottbus, GDR. Together with the conveyor belt system, the bridge weighs approximately 10,000 tons.

entry.dc:title: Use of Underfloor Drills in Open-Cast Mining.
entry.dc:creator: Schwate W.
entry.dc:description: The paper presents a review of the literature and discusses the investigations made to increase the capacity of rock drills. Application of underfloor drills in mining is also discussed.

entry.dc:title: STATUS OF THE SHELL-KOPPERS PROCESS.
entry.dc:creator: Vogt E.V.
entry.dc:description: This paper presents results of a semi-industrial study on the coal gasification performed in West Germany. A pilot plant with a capacity of 150t/d was used for gasification of low-caloric, low-cost coal feed, such as lignite and brown coal, available from open-cast mining. The possible future applications for this process are briefly reviewed. The gas produced (93-98% vol. hydrogen and carbon monoxide) is suitable for the manufacture of hydrogen or reducing gas and, with further processing, substitute natural gas (SNG). The gas also can be used for synthesizing ammonia, methanol and liquid hydrocarbons. Another possible application of this process is as an integral part of a combined-cycle power station featuring both gas and steam turbines. The integration of a Shell-Koppers coal gasifier with a combined-cycle power station will allow for electricity generation at 42-45% efficiency for a wide range of feed coals. Extensive test data are tabulated, plotted and evaluated. Economic considerations are included.

entry.dc:title: Changes in the geographical environment as a result of open mining.
entry.dc:creator: Kozacki L.
entry.dc:description: Discusses methods for forecasting changes in relief as a result of open-cast mining in the Konin coal basin (Poland) and the G.D.R. (East Germany). -P.Harris

entry.dc:title: (The anthropogene effects and their representation on maps on the area of the town Pecs).
entry.dc:creator: Erdosi F.
entry.dc:description: In the environs of Pecs, the effect of several production activities on waters, local climate, soils and vegetation have been examined. This study deals with the effects of coal mining, especially the recultivation of rock-debris, damage caused by surface movements, and the consequences of large-scale open-cast mining on the environment. -Eszter Turchanyi

entry.dc:creator: Olschowy G.
entry.prism:publicationName: Land Use and Landscape Planning Second Edition
entry.dc:description: A description of how Germany handles land reclamation after open-cast mining. Examines effects of open-cast mining on the landscape. -M.Brug-Chmielenska

entry.dc:title: FIELD EXPERIENCE OF EXTENDED OIL DRAIN INTERVAL IN OFF-HIGHWAY DIESEL ENGINES.
entry.dc:creator: Hosie R.
entry.dc:description: This paper describes an investigation into extension of engine oil drain intervals in a fleet of large off-highway vehicles engaged in open-cast mining operations. The results obtained indicate that with the particular engine/fuel/oil combination, unlimited oil drain intervals, excepting for severe contamination by fuel, coolant or abrasives, are practicable. As the potential oil savings are very substantial, the practice of unlimited oil drain interval is now proposed for all similar engines in the fleet.

entry.dc:title: Kansk-Achinsk Fuel and Energy Base.
entry.dc:creator: Mel'nikov N.
entry.dc:description: The role played by Siberia and the Far East in Soviet economy is reviewed and the place of the program of development of coal resources of the Kansk-Achinsk basin in its future growth is emphasized. Reserves of good quality coal in the basin are estimated at more than 450 Gt, including 140 Gt suitable for open-cast mining. Coal seams are mostly from 10-20 to 90 m thick and are horizontal or gently sloping. Stripping coefficient is from 0. 8 to 4 m**3/t. Ash content is from 6-13%, combustion heat 3200-3900 kcal/kg, sulfur content 0. 1-0. 9%, moisture content of fuel 31-39%. Three strip mines already in operation produced 27. 6 Mt of coal in 1975. Potential output of the basin as a whole may be 1 Gt/annum in the future. The first stage of development envisages an annual output of 250-300 Mt, the second stage 500-700 Mt. Various versions of the plan of construction of giant steam power plants envisage total plant capacities of 30, 50 and 70 MkW.

entry.dc:title: BROWN COAL MINING IN THE GERMAN DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC.
entry.dc:creator: McCombe C.
entry.dc:description: This article briefly discusses the brown-coal mining techniques used in the German Democratic Republic (GDR), the lignite deposits, and the manufacture of plant and equipment for open-cast mining. GDR currently mines more lignite than any other country in the world. A typical approach to the mining of brown coal in GDR involves the use of overburden bridges working in conjunction with bucket-ladder excavators.

entry.dc:title: Application of telecontrol engineering in lowering the ground water in open-cast mines.
entry.dc:creator: Winkler H.
entry.dc:description: The exploration and the mining of raw materials for the generation of energy are gaining an ever increasing importance. In the exploitation of raw materials by open-cast mining it is necessary to drain ground layers consisting of porous or jointed rocks. Otherwise the water will have an adverse effect on the static stability of slopes. The pumped volume of ground water per open-cast mine is considerable being in an order of magnitude of several cubic metres per second. In the past few years, after a scientific investigation of the geohydrological problem the lignite mining industry of the GDR introduced a new dewatering technology which, among other things, is implemented using modern automation equipment made by Kombinat VEB Elektro-Apparate-Werke, Berlin-Treptow. This dewatering technology is based on 200 to 800 filter wells per open-cast mine, the condition and the operation of which is monitored and controlled by remote control equipment of type ursatrans 4213 from a central control station. Ursatrans 4213 is a remote control system operating on a frequency time multiplex basis for the transmission of messages, measured values, and commands. The control station communicates with a maximum of 15 sub-stations, each of which is designed for the information volume of 60 filter wells. (A)
